generated_from: A state college catalog's Associate of Arts general education and graduation requirements, converted area by area. Real in shape and structure; the college, its catalog and its links are invented.

document.title: Associate of Arts — general education and graduation requirements
document.scope: The general education core and the graduation requirements for the AA. The 24 elective credits are unlisted by the source, and the college's wider course inventory is not covered.

other_requirements: Writing requirement (Gordon Rule): Composition I, Composition II and two further writing-credit courses, twelve credits in all, each at C or higher.
Mathematics competency: six credits of college-level mathematics at C or higher.
Civic literacy: pass National Government or either United States history course, and pass the Florida Civic Literacy Exam or an approved assessment.
Digital literacy: CGS1060C, an approved test, credit-by-exam or credit for prior learning, ideally within the first fifteen credits.
Foreign language competency, as prescribed in college policy.
At least a quarter of the prescribed college-level credits earned at the college.
A cumulative grade point average of 2.0 or higher.

additional_requirements.name: Writing requirement (Gordon Rule)
additional_requirements.rule: Composition I and Composition II, and two further writing-credit courses. A grade of C or higher is needed in each.

additional_requirements.name: Mathematics competency
additional_requirements.rule: Six credits of college-level mathematics at C or higher: either two courses from the Area 5 list, or one Area 5 course and one from the second list.
additional_requirements.notes: Coreq College Algebra may be taken in place of College Algebra, but not both. Precalculus Algebra and Trigonometry may replace Trigonometry and Pre Calculus Algebra together, and then a second course at or above College Algebra is still needed.

additional_requirements.name: Civic literacy
additional_requirements.rule: Depends on the effective catalog year. From Fall 2024: pass one of National Government, History of the United States to 1877, or History of the United States since 1877, and pass the Florida Civic Literacy Exam or an approved assessment.

additional_requirements.name: Digital literacy
additional_requirements.rule: Recommended within the first 15 credits: pass CGS1060C, an approved test, a credit-by-exam option, or credit for prior learning.

additional_requirements.name: Foreign language competency
additional_requirements.rule: As prescribed in college policy. The requirements page does not state the rule.

additional_requirements.name: Credits earned at the college
additional_requirements.rule: At least 25 per cent of the prescribed college-level credits must be earned here.

additional_requirements.name: Grade point average
additional_requirements.rule: A cumulative 2.0 or higher, including transfer credits in courses making up the degree.

data_notes: Braewood State College does not exist. The course data is real in shape and structure — the course numbering, the six general education areas and the sixty-credit degree are how a state college actually prints them — but the college and its documents are invented.
The Associate of Arts as the catalog prints it: 36 general education credits across six areas, plus 24 elective credits, for 60 in total.

The 24 elective credits carry no course list, because the source prints none — electives are described in prose as any college-level course outside preparatory and technical curricula. The requirement is recorded with an empty list rather than a guessed one.
Courses carry the marks the page puts against them, as flags: writing credit, which is what the Gordon Rule counts, and the several credit-by-exam and prior-learning routes.
Two rows are marked "(C)" and one "(I)", which are not among the codes the page defines. They are recorded as printed and noted on the course rather than guessed at.
One row, EUH1001, is printed with no title at all. The title here comes from the college's own course description page, and the course says so.

Prerequisites are empty throughout. The requirements page states them only in prose for a handful of courses, and a prerequisite tree that is right for a few courses and silent for the rest would be worse than none.

Every course is marked as available in either year, because the source says nothing about when a course is offered. The planner is set to two years of Fall, Spring and Summer, which is the shape of the degree rather than anything the page states.
Titles are readable forms of what the catalog prints in capitals; the printed form is kept in title_variants.
This is the 2025-2026 catalog year. Civic literacy in particular depends on a student's effective catalog year, and the rule recorded here is the one for Fall 2024 onward.
